pull.title: feat(harnesses): launch OpenCode, OpenCode 2 and Kilo without touching their config, and list every command per agent
pull.body:
## What this adds

Three coding agents MCC could already serve had no launcher: **OpenCode**, the
**OpenCode 2** preview (a separate `opencode2` binary that installs beside v1)
and **Kilo CLI**, which documents itself as a fork of OpenCode with the same
configuration. All three speak Anthropic Messages, so they reach MCC's existing
`POST /v1/messages` and need no new inbound surface.

`mcc-opencode`, `mcc-opencode2` and `mcc-kilo` are generated from the registry
added in #241 — console scripts, both installers' verification and summary
lists, both uninstallers' cleanup lists, `mcc-help`, and the Coding agents page.
No `fcc-` aliases: no installed copy of MCC ever published one, so inventing
them would ship commands that never had users.

## Zero-clobber: MCC owns a file, the user keeps theirs

These are the first harnesses that read provider configuration from a **file**
rather than from argv or env. Merging a block into
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` would make MCC a co-owner of a hand-written
document and leave a provider behind for anyone who stops using it. Each CLI
publishes a way out — an environment variable naming an *extra* config file
that joins the precedence chain rather than replacing it:

| Command | File MCC owns | Variable it is handed with | Documented at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mcc-opencode` | `~/.fcc/opencode-config.json` | `OPENCODE_CONFIG` | https://opencode.ai/docs/config/ — "Custom config is loaded between global and project configs in the precedence order", "Configuration files are merged together, not replaced" |
| `mcc-opencode2` | `~/.fcc/opencode2-config.json` | `OPENCODE_CONFIG` | same (verified against the v2 binary, below) |
| `mcc-kilo` | `~/.fcc/kilo-config.json` | `KILO_CONFIG` | https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/platforms/cli — "The Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode and supports the same configuration options" |

The user's own file is never read, written, merged or backed up. The file MCC
owns is created by the first `mcc-<id>` run — never at startup, so nothing is
scattered for a CLI you do not use — and refreshed by the existing fan-out
publisher afterwards.

**The token stays off disk.** The document writes `baseURL`, `apiKey` and an
`Authorization` header as OpenCode's own `{env:VARIABLE}` substitutions; the
launcher sets those two variables in the child process only.

The explicit `Authorization` header is not belt-and-braces. MCC authenticates
on `Authorization: Bearer` — the header Claude Code's `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`
produces (`api/dependencies.py:56`) — while `@ai-sdk/anthropic` sends
`x-api-key`, which MCC does not read. **Measured on OpenCode 1.18.25**: with
`apiKey` alone every request arrived at `POST /v1/messages` with no credential
and came back 401; adding the header made the same request 200.

## The serialiser

`application/catalogues/opencode.py`, one pure function shared by all three
harnesses (`format_id: "opencode"`), covered by the existing AST guard
`test_no_serialiser_hard_codes_a_limit`.

| Ladder field | OpenCode key |
| --- | --- |
| `context_length` | `limit.context` |
| `max_output_tokens` | `limit.output` |
| `reasoning.can_reason` | `reasoning` |
| `supports_tool_calls` | `tool_call` |
| `supports_vision` | `attachment` + `modalities.input` |
| `input_price` / `output_price` | `cost.input` / `cost.output` |
| `reasoning.supported_efforts` | `variants.<rung>`, clamped to OpenCode's own rungs |
| `default_parameters` | `options` |
| `provider_model_ref` (or the gateway id, for the no-thinking variant) | the model key, addressed as `mcc/<provider>/<model>` |

**Unknown stays unknown, in OpenCode's own idiom.** Every per-model key is
optional, and OpenCode's own fallback for an absent one is `0` — measured
against `opencode models --verbose` with a model declaring only a name. `0` is
exactly how models.dev, OpenCode's own model database, spells "not applicable
or unknown", and how MCC's own models.dev parser already reads it
(`providers/runtime/models_dev.py`). So an unknown limit is **omitted** rather
than invented, and every omission is recorded in `_mcc_defaulted`, on the
launcher's stderr and on the dashboard card.

One real generated fragment, from the scratch proxy:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "mcc": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/anthropic",
      "name": "My Claude Code",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "{env:MCC_OPENCODE_BASE_URL}",
        "apiKey": "{env:MCC_OPENCODE_API_KEY}",
        "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MCC_OPENCODE_API_KEY}" }
      },
      "models": {
        "llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5": {
          "name": "llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5",
          "limit": { "context": 200000, "output": 64000 },
          "reasoning": true,
          "attachment": true,
          "modalities": { "input": ["text", "image"], "output": ["text"] },
          "cost": { "input": 3.0, "output": 15.0 }
        },
        "llamacpp/gpt-4o-mini": {
          "name": "llamacpp/gpt-4o-mini",
          "limit": { "context": 128000, "output": 16384 },
          "reasoning": false,
          "attachment": true,
          "modalities": { "input": ["text", "image"], "output": ["text"] },
          "cost": { "input": 0.15, "output": 0.6 }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "_mcc_defaulted": {
    "llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5": ["tool_call", "cost.cache_read", "cost.cache_write"],
    "llamacpp/gpt-4o-mini": ["tool_call", "cost.cache_read", "cost.cache_write"]
  }
}
```

Two models, two different sets of numbers — the thing a fixed-placeholder
catalogue could not do. `tool_call` stays unknown because that gateway
publishes no `supported_parameters`, and says so rather than guessing `true`.

## Coding agents page: every command, per agent

The page already showed installed state, protocol and catalogue. It now also
lists **every command line each agent answers to** — the launcher, its
documented arguments, the legacy `fcc-` alias, the RTK toggles — each with a
one-line explanation and a copy button, all generated from
`config/harnesses.py` (new `HarnessInvocation` / `HarnessCommandLine`) rather
than restated in three prose pages that drift. `mcc-help` renders from the same
tuple, which removed the last hand-written special case in it
(`mcc-claude --discover-models` was hard-coded there).

As rendered (browser-driven, all with a working Copy button):

```
Claude Code   mcc-claude / mcc-claude --discover-models / mcc-claude -p "<prompt>"
              mcc-claude-old / fcc-claude / fcc-claude-old
              mcc-rtk enable claude / mcc-rtk disable claude
Codex CLI     mcc-codex / mcc-codex exec "<prompt>" / mcc-codex resume --last
              fcc-codex / mcc-rtk enable codex / mcc-rtk disable codex
Pi            mcc-pi / mcc-pi --version / fcc-pi
              mcc-rtk enable pi / mcc-rtk disable pi
OpenCode      mcc-opencode / mcc-opencode run "<prompt>" / mcc-opencode models mcc
              mcc-opencode -m mcc/<provider>/<model>
OpenCode 2    mcc-opencode2 / mcc-opencode2 run --standalone "<prompt>"
              mcc-opencode2 models
Kilo CLI      mcc-kilo / mcc-kilo run "<prompt>" / mcc-kilo models mcc
```

## Real-launch proof

Scratch MCC on **8199** with `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` redirected to a scratch home,
fed by a local OpenAI-compatible gateway on 8299 so the resolution ladder had
real answers to give. The live 8082 install was never written to or restarted.

```
$ HOME=<scratch> uv run mcc-opencode models mcc
My Claude Code: 2 model(s) publish no value for one or more fields, so OpenCode falls back to its own default:
  llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5: tool_call, cost.cache_read, cost.cache_write
  llamacpp/gpt-4o-mini: tool_call, cost.cache_read, cost.cache_write
mcc/llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5
mcc/llamacpp/gpt-4o-mini

$ HOME=<scratch> uv run mcc-opencode models mcc --verbose   # limits OpenCode actually holds
"limit": { "context": 200000, "output": 64000 }
"limit": { "context": 128000, "output": 16384 }
"cost":  { "input": 3, "output": 15,   "cache": { "read": 0, "write": 0 } }
"cost":  { "input": 0.15, "output": 0.6, "cache": { "read": 0, "write": 0 } }

$ HOME=<scratch> uv run mcc-opencode run --model mcc/llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5 "say ok"
> build - llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5
ok
exit=0
```

At the proxy, and one hop further upstream:

```
INFO:  127.0.0.1:17076 - "POST /v1/messages HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
gateway: chat request model= claude-sonnet-4-5
gateway: /v1/chat/completions "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 -
```

**OpenCode 2** — `@opencode-ai/cli@beta` = `0.0.0-beta-18743`, installed into a
scratch npm prefix, never into the user's globals:

```
$ HOME=<scratch> PATH=<scratch bin>:$PATH uv run mcc-opencode2 run --standalone --model mcc/llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5 "say ok"
> build - llamacpp/claude-sonnet-4-5
ok
exit=0
```

**Kilo** is not installed on this machine, so only the never-install path ran:

```
$ uv run mcc-kilo
Could not find Kilo CLI command: kilo
Install Kilo CLI with: npm install -g @kilocode/cli
```

## CONFIRMED vs UNVERIFIED

**CONFIRMED (a command was run, or the vendor's own doc was fetched)**

- `OPENCODE_CONFIG` points OpenCode at an MCC-owned file and merges rather than
  replaces — documented, and exercised on v1 `1.18.25` and v2 `0.0.0-beta-18743`.
- The per-model schema (`limit`, `cost`, `reasoning`, `tool_call`,
  `attachment`, `modalities`, `options`, `variants`) — read from the live
  `https://opencode.ai/config.json` schema and round-tripped through
  `opencode models --verbose`.
- OpenCode's fallback for an absent optional key is `0` for limits and costs,
  `true` for `tool_call`, `false` for `reasoning`/`attachment` — measured.
- `apiKey` alone does not authenticate against MCC; the `Authorization` header
  does — measured, 401 then 200.
- OpenCode 2 reads the same document and lists the same models; it needs
  `--standalone` because its background service keeps the config it started
  with — measured.
- `opencode` v1 `1.18.25` and `codex` are installed here; `opencode2` only in a
  scratch prefix; `kilo` is absent.

**UNVERIFIED**

- **Kilo's config was never loaded by a Kilo binary.** Its schema and
  `KILO_CONFIG` rest entirely on Kilo's own documentation, which states it is
  an OpenCode fork supporting the same options. Nobody ran `kilo` here.
- Whether `@ai-sdk/anthropic` honours a `variants.<rung>.reasoningEffort` body
  on the wire. MCC names only rungs the ladder published and invents no token
  budget, but the effect of selecting one was not measured.
- Whether OpenCode's own synthesised `high` / `max` thinking variants can be
  suppressed. For a reasoning model on `@ai-sdk/anthropic` OpenCode adds them
  itself from `limit.output`; MCC can decline to add rungs a model never
  claimed, but cannot remove OpenCode's two.
- RTK: all three ship `rtk_agent=False`. Whether RTK's shell-tool wrapper
  applies to OpenCode is unverified, and the registry's rule is that the flag
  is only set for an agent someone has confirmed.

## Browser drive

Chrome DevTools MCP against the scratch dashboard at `127.0.0.1:8199/admin`.
Screenshots in `screenshots-harness-pr4/`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Coding agents lists six harnesses | Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi, OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Kilo CLI |
| Installed probe | Claude/Codex/Pi/OpenCode **Installed**; OpenCode 2 and Kilo **Not installed**, each offering the vendor's own install line and no button that runs it |
| Full command list per harness | 8 / 6 / 5 / 4 / 3 / 3 rows, each with its one-line help and a Copy button |
| Copy button | clicking `mcc-opencode run "<prompt>"` wrote the clipboard and flipped the control to **Copied** |
| Catalogue readout after a launch | OpenCode: path `~/.fcc/opencode-config.json`, last written `2026-09-01T18:46:58.914770Z`, **Models 2**, `CLI defaults: 2 model(s)`; Kilo (never launched): "Never - written on the first mcc-kilo" |
| Config variable row | `OPENCODE_CONFIG` / `KILO_CONFIG` — "set for the launched process only, so your own config file is never edited" |
| Get Started launcher cards | 8 cards, now including OpenCode, OpenCode 2 and Kilo CLI |
| Console errors | none (one pre-existing a11y advisory, unrelated) |
| Layout | first pass overlapped the kind label with the absolutely-positioned copy button; row re-laid out as a single column with reserved padding and re-shot |

## Tests

New: `tests/application/test_opencode_serialiser.py` (12) and
`tests/cli/test_opencode_launcher.py` (5). Extended:
`test_harness_registry.py` (+5 contract tests, including
`test_installers_verify_every_registered_harness_command`, which compares both
installers *and* both uninstallers to the registry),
`test_serialiser_contract.py` (now shape-agnostic via a new
`model_entries(format_id, document)` helper, so a nested schema cannot dodge
the guards), `test_catalogue_fanout.py`, and four new jsdom cases.

```
uv run pytest -q --tb=line
15 failed, 8295 passed, 38 skipped

uv run pytest tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py -q -n 0
185 passed
```

The 15 are the standing baseline that also fails on unmodified `fork/main`: 8
websearch tests reading the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests,
and `test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`.

`uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run ruff check` clean over `src/` and
`tests/`; `uv run ty check` clean. Version 6.26.0 (MINOR) with `uv lock` in the
same commit.

## Deviations from the plan

- **`options.headers.Authorization` was added to the generated document.** The
  plan said auth would be MCC's `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` through `options.apiKey`;
  measurement showed that alone produces a 401 every time.
- **`mcc-opencode2 run` is documented and offered as `run --standalone`.** v2's
  background service caches the config it started with.
- **Unknown limits are omitted rather than filled from a CLI default.** The
  base rule says use the CLI's documented default where a field is required;
  OpenCode makes them all optional and its own fallback is `0`, which is
  models.dev's spelling of "unknown". Writing a made-up number would have been
  the invention the rule exists to prevent. Every omission is still recorded in
  `_mcc_defaulted`.

## Residual risks

- **Kilo is unverified end to end.** If its fork has diverged, `mcc-kilo` will
  produce a config Kilo ignores. It degrades to launching with no MCC provider
  rather than failing, and no user file is touched either way.
- **A `limit` MCC omits reads as `0` inside OpenCode**, which its context
  readout and compaction will treat as unknown. That is the honest state for a
  model nobody published a window for, but it is not a working ceiling.
- **Reasoning clamping is additive only.** OpenCode synthesises its own `high`
  and `max` variants for a reasoning model on `@ai-sdk/anthropic`; MCC cannot
  remove them, so a model whose ladder published only `low`/`medium` will still
  show OpenCode's two.
- **OpenCode 2 is a beta.** Its version string moves every build
  (`0.0.0-beta-18743` here) and its schema could diverge from v1 without notice;
  they share one serialiser today.
- **`opencode` on PATH is not proof it is OpenCode.** Unlike Pi, these three
  carry no `identity_help_markers`, so a same-named binary would be launched.
- The scratch verification used a local fake gateway for upstream metadata, not
  a paid provider; the numbers in the fragment above are models.dev's real
  answers for those model ids, resolved through MCC's own ladder.

commit.message:
feat(harnesses): launch OpenCode, OpenCode 2 and Kilo without touching their config, and list every command per agent

Three CLIs MCC could already serve had no launcher: OpenCode, its v2 preview
and Kilo, which is a fork of OpenCode and reads the same schema. All three
speak the Anthropic Messages protocol MCC already exposes at POST /v1/messages,
so nothing new was needed on the wire -- only a way to tell them where to send
it.

That "only" is the whole problem. Unlike Claude Code (two environment
variables), Codex (ephemeral -c assignments) and Pi (a process-local
extension), these three read provider configuration from a *file*. The obvious
implementation is to merge a provider block into the user's
~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, which would make MCC a co-owner of a document
they wrote by hand and would leave a block behind for anyone who stops using
it. Each CLI publishes a way out: an environment variable naming an *extra*
config file that joins its precedence chain rather than replacing it --
OPENCODE_CONFIG for OpenCode ("Custom config is loaded between global and
project configs in the precedence order",
https://opencode.ai/docs/config/) and KILO_CONFIG for Kilo, which documents
itself as a fork supporting the same options. So MCC writes a file of its own
under ~/.fcc and hands the launched process its path. Their file is never read,
written or backed up.

The proxy token is not in the generated file either. OpenCode resolves
{env:VARIABLE} substitutions inside a trusted config, so the document names two
variables and the launcher sets them in the child process only. It writes both
options.apiKey and an explicit Authorization header, and the second is not
belt-and-braces: MCC authenticates on Authorization: Bearer -- the header
Claude Code's own ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN produces -- while @ai-sdk/anthropic
sends x-api-key, which MCC does not read. Measured on OpenCode 1.18.25: with
apiKey alone every request reached POST /v1/messages carrying no credential and
came back 401; adding the header made the same request 200.

The new application/catalogues/opencode.py serialiser follows the rules the
Codex and Pi ones already obey. Ladder answers land in OpenCode's own keys --
limit.context, limit.output, reasoning, tool_call, attachment plus
modalities.input, cost.input/output, options from the gateway's pinned
parameters, and one variants entry per reasoning rung the model actually
published, clamped to OpenCode's vocabulary and never extended. Unknown stays
unknown in OpenCode's own idiom: every per-model key is optional, and OpenCode's
fallback for an absent one is 0 -- which is exactly how models.dev, its own
model database, spells "not applicable or unknown", and how MCC's models.dev
parser already reads it. So an unknown limit is omitted rather than invented,
and every omission is recorded under _mcc_defaulted, printed on the launcher's
stderr and counted on the dashboard card.

The Coding agents page now also answers "what can I actually type". Each card
lists every command line the agent responds to -- the launcher, its documented
arguments, the legacy fcc- alias, the RTK toggles -- each with a one-line
explanation and a copy button, all generated from config/harnesses.py rather
than restated in three doc pages that drift. mcc-help is generated from the
same tuple, which removed the last hand-written special case in it.

Verification. Scratch MCC on 8199 with HOME redirected, fed by a local
OpenAI-compatible gateway so the ladder had real answers: mcc-opencode wrote
~/.fcc/opencode-config.json, printed which fields nobody published, and
`opencode models mcc --verbose` reported limit {context: 200000, output: 64000}
and cost {input: 3, output: 15} for one model and {context: 128000, output:
16384} / {0.15, 0.6} for the other -- two models, two different answers, which
is the thing the old fixed-placeholder catalogues could not do.
`mcc-opencode run "say ok"` returned "ok" with POST /v1/messages 200 at the
proxy. mcc-opencode2 did the same against @opencode-ai/cli 0.0.0-beta-18743
installed in a scratch prefix, with --standalone: v2 runs a background service
that keeps the config it started with, which is now documented and is the
argument form the dashboard offers. Kilo is not installed here, so only its
exit-127 install hint was exercised; its schema rests on Kilo's own
documentation, not on a run.

Full suite 8295 passed, 15 pre-existing failures that also fail on unmodified
fork/main; jsdom suite 185 passed alone with -n 0. Browser-driven on the
Coding agents page: six cards, correct installed states, full command lists
with working copy buttons, catalogue path, timestamp and model count, zero
console errors.

test(installers): give the fake uv the three new shims it must create

The installer contract tests stand up a fake `uv tool install` that writes one
stub per published command, then let the real installer verify its own list.
Adding mcc-opencode, mcc-opencode2 and mcc-kilo to that list without adding
them to the fake made the verification correctly fail: the installer looked for
shims the stub never wrote.

It passed locally because every install.sh test *skips* on Windows -- 20 skips
in that file here -- so the POSIX half of this suite proves nothing on this
machine and only CI saw it.
